sources.citation: Bracks, Christoph. 2025. glossing abbreviations for the Masep dictionary). ELAR session mvs0130. 2 pp.

sources.note: Consonant and vowel tables from Foley 2018; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Bracks, Christoph. 2025 (2025-10-28). The Masep Language Archive: collection guide / Panduan arsip (Metadocumentation_0737). ELAR, Masep Language Documentation Project IPF0421 (ELDP postdoctoral fellowship 2023-2025). 9 pp.
sources.note: Only an orthography table (p. 6-7: Indonesian orthography = IPA except c=[tʃ], j=[dʒ], b=[β], ng=[ŋ], ny=[ɲ], y=[j]); segmentation into Intonation Units; says head-mounted-mic recordings 'are thus very valuable for prosodic/phonetic research'; states a grammar sketch is in progress. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Bracks, Christoph. 2025. Masep dictionary, preliminary version, ELAR session mvs0130 'Dictionary and FLEx Database / Kamus dan Database FLEx'. 99 pp.
sources.note: FLEx lexicon export (Prince XML) with photos, Indonesian and English glosses; no introduction or phonology note; headwords in practical orthography with no stress marks (0 IPA stress marks, 0 acute accents in the text).

sources.citation: Bracks, Christoph. 2025. Massep_20251027.fwbackup (FLEx database of the Masep lexicon and glossed texts), ELAR session mvs0130.
sources.note: Open-access FLEx backup behind the dictionary; could contain phonological notes or stress-marked forms not exported to the PDF (the PDF has none).

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes 'Mark Donohue has collected enough data for sketches of.. Masep [mvs].. (p.c. 2008)'.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. 18 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 4.1 Masep (p. 6): 'the language has an unusual phonological system, with a skewing in the distributions of stops and consonants' plus a tentative phoneme chart (t c kw k~q, j, g, Φ s S, Β Γ, m n ɲ, w r y; i u e o a) and a note on syllabic r; nothing on stress or tone for Masep (the only 'stressed schwa' remark, p. 9, concerns Airoran/Samarokena).

sources.citation: Hurd, Fred. 1979. Massep. Unpublished word list, ms., SIL (4 pp.), as transcribed in Wiktionary, 'Appendix:Massep word list' (175 items, orthographic + phonetic columns).
sources.note: No statement; the phonetic column carries survey-style stress apostrophes. My automatic tabulation : 146 marked forms, stress on initial syllable 70, penult 76, final 10 (disyllables counted in both initial and penult; trisyllables: initial 36, second 31, final 3). Pattern is mixed initial/penultimate, not decisive.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy & Mark Donohue. n.d. Masep. New Guinea World (Santa Fe Institute), West Foja Range.
sources.note: Phonology section reproduces Clouse, Donohue & Ma (2002: 6) inventory (16-17 consonants, 5 vowels), reinterpreting c j as tʃ dʒ from Donohue's 1998 transcriptions; no mention of stress, accent or tone. Lists unpublished sources: Donohue 1998 survey vocabulary; Erickson n.d. and Silen n.d. survey vocabularies.

sources.citation: Bracks, Christoph Alexander. 2025. Sketch Grammar / Sketsa Tata Bahasa. ELAR, Masep Language Documentation Project (IPF0421), session mvs500. Work in progress; keywords Phonetics, Phonology, Prosody.

sources.note: The only grammatical description of Massep ever written, by the ELDP documenter (2023-2025 fieldwork, ~30 speakers); its keywords include Phonology and Prosody, so a stress/accent statement is likely here.
